script.title: The History of the Henry Fingerprint Classification System
script.description: In late 19th-century Bengal, an administrative and mathematical method was developed to index fingerprints. This system contributed to the transition away from body measurements in forensic science. Here is the background of the system involving Qazi Azizul Haque, Hem Chandra Bose, and Edward Henry.

scenes.narration: A classification method once assisted in organizing fingerprint records.
In 1890s Bengal, investigators used body measurements to track offenders.
Inspector General Edward Henry ordered fingerprint collection alongside body measurements in 1896.
Fingerprint records were gathered, creating a need for a structured sorting method.
Indian officer Qazi Azizul Haque devised a mathematical formula using 1,024 pigeonholes.
Scholar Hem Chandra Bose refined the method with detailed fingerprint sub-classifications.
An 1897 official committee evaluated fingerprinting, leading to changes in identification methods.
The contributors received British government recognition years later for their work.
This classification system influenced forensics—how do you view this history?
